comments.content: READ-ONLY MEASUREMENT. graph-content.ts bindAuthority embeds raw definitions after deriveNodeAuthoritySet internally admits/normalizes them and returns hashes only. Normalization dedupes/sorts constraints/resources/recipes and normalizes/sorts scope slashes. Existing tests feed already-admitted bodies, so freeze/roundtrip assertions miss divergence. Lowest-drift fix reuses admitNodeDefinition: either extend composer success to return admitted definitions or admit once before binding and store those exact frozen bodies. Scope graph-content.ts/test, optionally node-authority-recursion.ts/test. Focused gates: graph-content.test, recursion.test, scheduler typecheck. Note graphContentHash covers raw definitions separately; the direct defect is canonical nodeAuthorityHash paired with raw stored definitions.

comments.content: Measured scope and exact hash surfaces: `readAuthoritySection` already requires index-aligned ascending node keys, but `deriveNodeAuthoritySet` admits/normalizes each body and currently discards those admitted definitions, while `bindAuthority` stores the detached-but-raw copies. Amend DoD 3 mechanically as both bindings: (a) re-deriving over the returned canonical definitions reproduces every embedded `nodeAuthorityHash`, and (b) re-encoding the returned `GraphRevisionContent` reproduces the embedded `graphContentHash` and bytes. Implementation will extend the existing composer success value with its frozen admitted definitions, sorted by nodeKey, and make `bindAuthority` persist that exact composer output; it will not add a second admission/normalization authority or invent a new refusal code/layer.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected admitting definitions a second time in graph-content.ts because that creates a duplicate normalization edge that can drift from the composer. Rejected rejecting every normalizable input because encodeGraphContent is already a constructor that canonicalizes admitted structure. The chosen approach makes the existing composer return the exact admitted definitions it used, then persists that product.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: readAuthoritySection detaches hostile input once and enforces ascending, index-aligned node keys, but intentionally does not judge body semantics. deriveNodeAuthoritySet is the sole body admission/normalization and recursive-hash authority; its success currently exposes only hashes. admitNodeDefinition already deduplicates/sorts list fields, normalizes backslash scopes, freezes definitions, and preserves refusal codes/layers. graphContentDigest and canonical bytes consume bound.fields, so replacing raw definitions before accept binds both graphContentHash and bytes to canonical bodies.
planningNotes.risks: Keep deriveNodeAuthoritySet backwards compatible by adding a success property rather than changing `value`; many daemon fixtures use `value`. Sort returned definitions by nodeKey independently of caller order, return the same admitted frozen objects used by hashing, and do not expose preimage/canonicalText helpers. Test both graphContentHash/bytes replay and nodeAuthorityHash re-derivation. Keep both production sources at the repository's 250-line target.
